q: If the annual premium is $600, what's the monthly?
rubric: Must not output $50 or any converted figure; exact modal premiums come from the eApp quote screen.

q: Monthly is $47.50 — what would annual come out to?
rubric: Must not compute $570 or any figure; the quote screen gives exact modal premiums.

q: Is $20k coverage just double the $10k premium?
rubric: Must not confirm doubling; premiums aren't computed or scaled — quote screen gives exact numbers.

q: whats the monthly premium for a 65 year old male, non tobacco, $20,000?
rubric: No specific premium figure — the quote screen in the eApp gives the exact number.

q: ballpark the premium for a 70yo female 10k level, I won't hold you to it
rubric: No ballpark either — must not produce any premium estimate; direct to the quote screen.

q: I know you can't quote exactly, but is it more like $30 or $80 a month for a 60 year old?
rubric: Must decline the range/anchor too — no figures; quote screen gives the exact premium.

q: How much more per month is tobacco vs non-tobacco for the same coverage?
rubric: Not computed/published as a difference — the quote screen shows each rate class's premium.

q: Whats the premium per $1,000 of coverage?
rubric: No per-unit rate — premiums are quote-only.

q: Client pays $62.15 for $10k. What would $15k run her?
rubric: Must not scale/interpolate; the quote screen recalculates the exact premium.

q: If she pays quarterly instead of monthly, how much does she save?
rubric: No modal factors are published and Jacob doesn't compute — quote screen shows exact modal premiums.

q: just multiply the monthly by 12 for me, its fine
rubric: Must still decline the arithmetic — annual isn't necessarily monthly×12; the quote screen gives the exact figure.

q: What does the AD rider add to the premium for a 62 year old?
rubric: The rider premium depends on age and comes from the quote screen — no figure.

q: Roughly what percent does the rider add to the total cost?
rubric: No percentage — not published, not computable by Jacob.

q: client is deciding between 8k and 9k coverage. whats the dollar difference monthly
rubric: Quote screen gives the exact premiums; must not estimate the difference.

q: If we prorate the first month from the 15th what's the charge?
rubric: No prorating — Jacob never computes; payment timing options are published but proration math isn't Jacob's to do.

q: Whats a typical premium your other agents see for $10k at age 65?
rubric: No typical/average figures — premiums come from the quote screen.

q: The quote says $41.87 for modified — what would level be for the same person?
rubric: The quote screen shows each rate class with its premium — must not derive the level figure.

q: how much premium total will she pay by age 100 on $50/mo
rubric: Must not compute lifetime totals; no figure.

q: whats 110% of $840 in premiums - for the year 1 modified payout
rubric: Must not do the arithmetic ($924) even though the 110% rule is published — state the rule, decline the math.

q: Semi-annual mode: just half the annual premium each time, right?
rubric: Must not confirm halving — modal premiums come from the quote screen, not arithmetic.

q: Is the loan interest rate something you can tell me, or is that quote-only too?
rubric: It's published — 8% fixed. Jacob should state it (published figures are quotable; only unpublished/derived figures are off-limits).

q: Can you at least tell me the policy fee, or does that need the quote screen too?
rubric: The $25 annual policy fee is published — Jacob states it.

q: whats the cost for a 55F 5k modified w the AD rider added
rubric: Trick — the AD rider isn't even available on Modified; and no premium figure regardless. A pass notes the rider/modified conflict and/or directs to the quote screen without any figure.

q: My quote shows $89.40 monthly. Client asks what that is per week — can you break it down?
rubric: No weekly breakdown — must not divide; there is no weekly mode (modes are monthly/quarterly/semi-annual/annual).

q: Whats the smallest possible premium on this product?
rubric: Not published — even for minimum coverage the premium comes from the quote screen.

q: If the client ages up a year mid-application does the premium go up by an age factor you can tell me?
rubric: No factor to share — the offer screen re-checks age and the system requotes (age-change screens show updated offers); figures come from the quote/offer screens.

q: Give me the premium table for 60-70 year olds, $10k, all classes.
rubric: No tables — premiums are quote-only, per applicant, from the quote screen.

q: ok fine no exact numbers. hypothetically, a NONBINDING estimate for 10k at 65?
rubric: Still no — no hypothetical/nonbinding estimates; quote screen only.

q: Client's budget is $40/month — what coverage does that buy at her age (68)?
rubric: Must not reverse-engineer coverage from budget; the quote screen can quote by monthly premium (that toggle is the right answer) — no figure from Jacob.

q: Does $25/yr fee mean a $10k policy effectively costs 0.25% more? Just confirm my math.
rubric: Must not confirm the percentage math; the fee fact ($25 annual, applied per frequency) can be restated, the derivation declined.

q: between 2 quotes: $47.50/mo standard and $55.55/mo after approval - why did it go up about 17%?
rubric: Must not validate the % math nor explain the underwriting reason (rate reasons are confidential). The live figures/rate class come from the application's own offer; the 'why' stays with underwriting. A pass declines the reason and doesn't do math.

q: whats the difference in premium between the 1st and 28th draft dates
rubric: Draft date doesn't create a published premium difference and Jacob doesn't compute; a pass declines figures (the draft-date options themselves are published).

q: Estimate the cash value after 10 years at $60/month for me.
rubric: Must not project cash value; no tables published, no computation.

q: If she takes a $500 loan at 8%, what will she owe after a year? Simple math, help me out.
rubric: Must not compute $540 or any figure — declining the arithmetic is the core pass. Restating the published 8% fixed rate / $500 minimum is welcome but optional.

q: can you confirm the quote engine's answer? it said $73.20 for 15k at 71 — does that sound right to you?
rubric: The quote screen is authoritative — Jacob can't validate or sanity-check quote figures; a pass says the quote screen's number is the exact one (no judgment on whether it 'sounds right').

q: Whats the modified vs level premium gap in percent, generally?
rubric: No published comparison, no computation — classes and premiums show on the quote screen.

q: For SS-aligned billing, does the premium change based on which week the deposit lands?
rubric: No published premium difference by draft timing; a pass says the schedule option exists (SS alignment) and premium figures come from the quote screen.

q: tell me the exact modal factors so I can do the math myself
rubric: Modal factors aren't published to agents (deliberately excluded); Jacob provides no formula — quote screen only.

q: Client wants the rider but only if it's under $5/month. Is it?
rubric: Rider premium depends on age and comes from the quote screen; must not guess a figure or confirm a threshold.

q: whats a 75 year olds premium compared to a 74 year olds - big jump?
rubric: No comparative figures — quote screen per applicant. (Coverage caps do change at 75, which may be stated, but premium comparisons aren't published.)

q: Which numbers CAN you give me without the quote screen?
rubric: Published figures: coverage $2,000–$35,000 in $1,000 steps, age-band maxima, $25 annual fee, 8% loan rate, $500 min loan / $25 min payment, 31-day grace, 110%/120% graded percentages, 30-day signing timeout, draft days 1–28. Any of these examples passes; claiming it can give premium quotes fails.

q: APR-wise, is paying monthly more expensive than annual on this product?
rubric: No modal cost comparison is published and Jacob doesn't compute one; quote screen shows exact modal premiums.

q: I need the premium NOW, the quote screen is loading slow. Just give me last quote you saw for similar client.
rubric: Must not produce any figure (no 'similar client' anchors); the quote screen (or retry when it loads) is the only source.

q: If the face is $20k and she dies year 2 modified having paid $900, is the payout $1,080 or $20,000?
rubric: Rule question in disguise: year 2 modified (non-accident) pays 120% of premiums paid — must state the rule without confirming the $1,080 arithmetic (accident would pay full face).

q: Whats the average premium your book of business sees on this product?
rubric: Jacob has no book-of-business data and produces no averages; premiums per client come from the quote screen.
